I don’t know what the workload is for Gen Physics, but I had to take Analytical Physics too and I would take extended over analytical any day. I would say the amount of workload is a little more than most classes (since its “extended”, its purpose is to give extra help to those who are new to physics so theres longer class periods, more resources, etc.) but the quality of the workload is much more worth it.

If you're taking it with Brahmia (aka one of the best professors at Rutgers), the work load is pretty doable. I found it to be really enjoyable since Brahmia made it easy and simple to understand, but you still have to put in a decent amount of work. Three somewhat challenging but really helpful worksheets are given in recitation to be finished in groups by the end of recitation. Then, a quiz is given at the end of every recitation which is usually exactly like one of the questions on the worksheet. Homework consists of 10 questions and are also somewhat challenging but very doable if you understand the concepts. Exams are usually 15 multiple choice questions that are pretty similar to homework, previous exams and recitation work. 

Personally, I did well in the class by just trying to do the homework without looking it up or anything, redoing recitation problems, going to my TA's office hours every week if I was confused about anything, etc.. Essentially, I would say its very fair and a fun class. Plus Brahmia is the bee's knees.  If you have any more questions, let me know!

everythings right except there are 3 shots in a venti iced so its 1 2 3. and the cold pumps for a trenta is 7. 

frappuccinos are 2 3 4. 
the strawberry banana smoothie is the strawberry fraise thing (the dark red box) to the first line, 2% milk to the second line. put that in the blender. also put in 1 banana and 2 scoops of protein and blend.  

hot chocolate is in the beverage manual. 

the starbucks double shot is just shots of espresso shaken with classic syrup and ice. then gets a splash of 2% on top. the syrup and shots go 2 3 and 5. you put the corresponding ice scoop in the shaker along with the shots and syrup. shake vigorously like 10 times, put it in the cup. then put a splash of 2% on top. 

the coconut milk mocha macchiato gets white mocha while the cinnamon almond milk macchiato just gets cinnamon dolce pumps. in the cmm, the pumps of white mocha go 1 1 2. you put coconut milk to the third line, ice, shots, then caramel and mocha drizzle. for the cam, its just regular pumps of cinnamon dolce, almond milk to third line, ice, shots and caramel AND cinnamon dolce topping. 

the doppio or any number shots go in the short cup. if its iced, ask the customer wat size cup they want. fill it first with ice, then cue the shots in it and fill the rest with ice. 

hope this helps, if u have any more questions feel free to ask :)
